RagShortTexts: The standing military of Geats in 374 AD relied upon veteran formations specialized in disciplined field deployment.
Combining heavy protective armor with specialized assault weaponry, the troops executed tactical doctrines honed in frontier engagements.
Commanders emphasized coordinated shock charges and defensive stability, preventing frontline collapse against aggressive cavalry raids.

Variants.Content: The martial renown of Geats rested upon exhaustive drilling and veteran battlefield cohesion during the turbulent close of the 4th century. Core tactical doctrine integrated heavy shield formations with disciplined skirmishing wings, executing tactical maneuvers designed to absorb and counter enemy shock. Along vulnerable sectors, defensive engineers implemented field fortifications and obstacles, breaking the initial momentum of hostile assaults. Once enemy ranks faltered, armored shock reserves counter-charged under thunderous horn blasts, crushing exposed flanks with heavy swords and barbed spears. This balance of resilient endurance and ferocious striking power formed the military bedrock preserving Geats against overwhelming regional adversaries.

Ash spears level and shield rims lock, and the front ranks wait for the drums. Warhorses must be absorbed by shoulders braced against each other and the rear files thrust through any opening. A man who lets his shield drop for a moment is trampled, and the sergeant's watchword is the only order anyone can hear over the screaming.

Riders ferry orders from the ridge, where field commanders wait by the standards. Victory depends on keeping the baggage column moving through wet roads and holding the infantry center until the shock reserve can be unleashed. Once the enemy line breaks, the mounted wings will pour into its flank. Every chieftain keeps a tally of whose men were sacrificed.
